title: FreeRTOS on Arduino-ESP32: sensor task and queue

spans.text: Goal: apply “FreeRTOS on Arduino-ESP32: sensor task and queue” to a real program or device. The key principle is: The queue copies each reading by value; the sensor task sends twice a second and `loop()` prints received items. Replace `A0` with an ADC-capable pin on the exact board. In a project, follow this guidance: Practical sequence: create the queue, check task creation, read the sensor in the task, send with a timeout, receive in `loop()`, and define full-queue behavior. Use `xTaskCreatePinnedToCore` only for a measured reason; pinning does not automatically make work faster. ESP-IDF SMP scheduling and Arduino-ESP32 API behavior depend on version.
QUESTION: What will this example do? Predict the result first.
Serial Monitor prints timestamped ADC readings from the queue; values depend on the sensor and board.

Arduino-ESP32 Core includes the FreeRTOS kernel; no separate RTOS library is required. A sensor task puts readings into a queue, and `loop()` receives and prints them. This separates acquisition from output and avoids an unprotected shared variable. A classic UNO's standard sketch environment does not provide the same task API; check for a compatible RTOS port and its memory cost on other boards.
